paper_id: Discriminative Neural Sentence Modeling by Tree-Based Convolution__oa_W2963872035
title: Discriminative Neural Sentence Modeling by Tree-Based Convolution
motivation: CNN捕捉局部特征但不捕获结构；RNN捕获结构但路径长导致梯度消失
problem_framing: 如何利用句子结构同时保持短传播路径
key_insight: 树结构上应用固定深度子树的特征检测器，所有节点到输出层路径等长
method_signature: 树卷积核滑动过整棵语法树，max pooling聚合特征
evaluation_criteria: 情感分析与问题分类的准确率
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: c-TBCNN略逊于d-TBCNN；复杂pooling效果有限；c-TBCNN的3-slot pooling是暂时硬编码
evidence_for_taste: CNNs do not capture inherent sentence structures
RNNs may have difficulties in learning deep dependencies
A curious question is whether we can combine
d-TBCNN achieves higher performance than c-TBCNN
TBCNNs are not very sensitive to pooling methods
complicated pooling methods do preserve more information to some extent, but the effect is not large
thinking_moves: 从CNN和RNN各自的缺陷反推设计需求
将位置编码改为依赖类型编码以处理变长子节点
先理论分析传播路径长度，再实验验证长句效果差距
cites_own_work: Mou et al. (2014) arXiv TBCNN: A tree-based convolutional neural network for programming language processing
